messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: metering.alert.token_count_drift triggered for EU region at 09:03 UTC. Delta over threshold (25%) across emitters. Paging oncall.
laura-sre: I'm on it. Any customer-facing alerts yet?
maria-support: A few customers saw overage flags and emailed support. No billing charges posted yet, just flags in UI.
laura-sre: Ok. First check: are ingesters/backpressure ok? raj-ml can you look at token-aggregation service metrics?
raj-ml: Looking. token-aggregator show steady input but output to billing-queue dropped ~09:00. Kafka lag spiked on partition 4.
ops-jordan: Confirming: we had a brief controller GC + disk flush on the EU emitter host (emitter-eu-3) at 08:58, coincides with Kafka rebalance. Might be NFS snapshot I/O waiting.
laura-sre: That explains lag. Does the aggregator retry correctly or are tokens counted twice later?
raj-ml: Risk: aggregator uses at-least-once semantics, but downstream dedupe window is 10s. If messages were buffered and re-emitted after >10s, dedupe missed -> double-count risk.
maria-support: Customers are seeing overage flags (UI) because the billing validator saw anomalous count bumps. No invoices yet. We should prevent further flags where possible.
laura-sre: Action plan:
1) Pause emitter-eu-3 publish to billing-queue (safe fallback) -> ops
2) Backfill consumer to reprocess with dedupe-key enrichment -> raj
3) Pause alerting on overage flags (support) until triage completes -> maria
Please ack when started.
ops-jordan: Pausing emitter-eu-3 -> applied feature-flag emitter.publish=false on emitter-eu-3. Confirmed stop of new publishes. :white_check_mark:
maria-support: Paused customer overage notifications in Support UI for affected orgs (rolled to 3 orgs so far). Sent temp email to affected customers: "We are investigating anomalous usage flags; no billing changes pending." :envelope:
raj-ml: Starting backfill job with stricter dedupe (hash + timestamp window 5m) to avoid double-counting. Kickoff command:
```
./backfill --topic billing-queue-eu --from-offset 124500 --to-latest --dedupe-window=300
```
laura-sre: Nice. Monitor token_delta distribution and report when tail drops below 2% variance.
raj-ml: Early progress: consumer caught up ~50k msgs, dedupe reduced duplicates by ~92% compared to naive replay. Estimated remaining window 18m.
ops-jordan: Found root cause: nightly backup I/O on emitter-eu-3 kicked the JVM into long-GC, which held Kafka producer threads; producers batched and re-sent after GC -> duplicates + delayed metrics. Will adjust backup window and bump producer linger.
laura-sre: Good find. Long-term: add producer-side idempotency and extend dedupe key TTL. Short-term: keep emitter paused until backfill stable.
maria-support: Support notified customers that flags will be cleared automatically once billing counts reconcile. I've logged ticket with billing-eng for any manual clears.
billing-eng: Acknowledge. We'll refrain from finalizing invoices for affected customers until counts reconcile. If any org needs manual credit, escalate to finance.
laura-sre: Status update in 20m or when backfill completes. Thanks everyone. :pray:
incidents-bot: Incident assigned: INCIDENT-2026-3869 (token-window-slippage). Severity: P2. Handoff: laura-sre -> oncall rotation at 10:00 UTC.
laura-sre: Handing off monitoring to next-oncall at 10:00. Current mitigation: emitter paused, backfill in progress, support notifications paused, billing hold in place. Will update if duplicates remain or if customer impact grows.
raj-ml: Backfill finished at 10:12 UTC. Final dedupe pass shows net token delta normalized; duplicates accounted for ~1.8% residual variance.
maria-support: Cleared temporary overage flags for impacted customers and sent follow-up email explaining root cause and remediation plan. No chargebacks required.
ops-jordan: Implemented config change: move EU backup window from 08:55 -> 03:00 UTC and increased producer.idempotence.enabled=true for emitter pool.
laura-sre: Closing incident in 30m if metrics stable. Documenting postmortem notes and action items. Thanks team. :tada:
